extracted.intended_audience: developers and advanced users who want to obtain, build, install, or contribute to the GAP computational algebra system
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for obtaining GAP (stable or development), installing required dependencies, building GAP from source, bootstrapping and building packages, and contributing to the GAP repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain a stable release
rubrics_metrics.description: The latest stable release of the GAP system can be obtained from https://www.gap-system.org/install/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After downloading a stable release, follow the instructions in the file INSTALL.md in the GAP root directory. Most users should use the latest official release rather than a development version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a development version (clone repository)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use a development version of GAP, clone the GAP source repository using git: git clone https://github.com/gap-system/gap
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Development versions require additional software dependencies for compilation; only use a development version if you need the latest changes. The development version does not come bundled with all GAP packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required build dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: You need at least these: a C compiler (e.g. GCC or Clang), a C++ compiler, GNU Make, GNU Autoconf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are minimum requirements to compile GAP from source. Missing these will prevent building the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended optional dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended development headers (optional but advised): GMP (GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library), zlib, GNU Readline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not install these, GAP will either build its own copies (slowing compilation) or omit certain features. Example install commands: On Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf libgmp-dev libreadline-dev zlib1g-dev; Fedora: sudo dnf install gcc gcc-c++ make autoconf gmp-devel readline-devel zlib-devel; Alpine: sudo apk add build-base autoconf gmp-dev readline-dev zlib-dev.

rubrics_metrics.name: macOS dependency installation options
rubrics_metrics.description: On macOS, dependencies can be installed using Homebrew, Fink, or MacPorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Homebrew: brew install autoconf gmp readline; Fink: fink install autoconf2.6 gmp5 readline7; MacPorts: port install autoconf gmp readline. See INSTALL.md for additional macOS hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build procedure (generate configure and build)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run ./autogen.sh to generate the configure script, then proceed as described in INSTALL.md. If everything goes well, start GAP by executing ./gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the steps in INSTALL.md in the GAP root directory. The README refers to a recommended order: autogen.sh → follow INSTALL.md → run ./gap to start the built system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining and bootstrapping GAP package distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The development version does not include all GAP packages; bootstrap stable versions of packages if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: make bootstrap-pkg-minimal or make bootstrap-pkg-full. Note that make bootstrap-pkg-full only unpacks packages and does not build those that require compilation. To build packages, change to the pkg directory and call ../bin/BuildPackages.sh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions and developer guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The GAP Project welcomes contributions of code, documentation, blog posts, or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contributions to this repository, read the contributor guidelines. Additional information includes Developer guidelines and Notes on the build system. Follow repository CONTRIBUTING.md and DEVELOPING.md before submitting changes or pull requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep up to date on GAP news or ask questions, use the GAP forum, GAP development mailing lists, GitHub notifications, or Slack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about working with GAP, ask them on the GAP forum mailing list (requires subscription) or use one of the various support channels linked from the project site.
